prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1404; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened on a sideswipe during a lane change. The insured reported that the other vehicle drifted into their lane as they were merging, and the claimant's representing attorney has requested that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is listed as a named driver and the vehicle was covered at the time of loss. Damage to the vehicle is consistent with the reported impact, and the police report, scene photos, and the other driver's statement all describe the collision the same way.

Entry 3: Police and independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation so far, including the initial recorded statement and the follow-up call through counsel.

Entry 4: Medical records describe a neck strain, which fits the type and force of a side impact of this kind. No prior treatment to the neck or upper back appears in the records we have obtained so far.

Entry 5: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy that tapered as the claimant's symptoms improved and the treating provider noted steady progress. A neighbor mentioned seeing the vehicle with prior body damage several weeks before the claimed date, so I am following up on that comment to see whether it can be verified or ruled out.

Entry 6: No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files or in prior claim history, and the repair estimate matches the damage shown in the photos. Pending the outcome of the neighbor follow-up, the file remains open with the injury evaluation in progress.
